question: Why did the Andy Warhol Foundation stop ruling on which Warhols are genuine in 2012?
answer: Because saying no had become too costly. Collectors whose pictures the foundation's authentication board rejected took it to court, one alleging a conspiracy to control the Warhol market. The foundation won, but legal costs reportedly reached about $10 million. The board had run since 1995; after it closed, owners had one fewer place to ask.
move: When judging costs more than staying silent, expect the judges to go quiet.
